recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中纖維化的骨髓腔內有成群、呈放射狀（花瓣狀，rosette）排列的無色透明、折光性棒狀結晶，周圍有多核異物型巨細胞（foreign body giant cell）包圍，偏光下呈明亮雙折射，這些是草酸鈣結晶（oxalosis）的線索。
features: Clusters of colorless to pale grey, refractile, rod- and plate-shaped crystals arranged in radiating rosette (floret-like) aggregates within marrow spaces
Crystal aggregates rimmed by multinucleated foreign-body-type giant cells and histiocytes
Marrow spaces replaced by loose fibrocellular stroma with spindle cells; hematopoiesis largely absent in the field
Irregularly thickened bony trabeculae around the fibrotic spaces
Reticulin stain: markedly increased, dense reticulin fiber network surrounding the crystal deposits
Polarized light: crystals are strongly birefringent in radiating sheaf-like aggregates
describe_en: Bone marrow trephine biopsy shows irregularly thickened bony trabeculae enclosing marrow spaces replaced by fibrocellular stroma, with only a small residual focus of hematopoietic cells. Within the fibrotic marrow are multiple aggregates of colorless, refractile, rod- and plate-shaped crystals arranged in radiating rosettes, surrounded by a foreign-body giant cell and histiocytic reaction. A reticulin stain demonstrates markedly increased reticulin fibrosis around the deposits, and the crystals are strongly birefringent under polarized light. Findings are consistent with marrow oxalosis (calcium oxalate crystal deposition) with secondary myelofibrosis, in keeping with primary hyperoxaluria in the appropriate clinical setting.

ddx.vs: PMF shows reticulin/collagen fibrosis with atypical clustered megakaryocytes but no birefringent crystal deposits or foreign-body giant cell reaction.
Renal osteodystrophy produces peritrabecular fibrosis with increased osteoclastic resorption and osteoid, but lacks rosettes of polarizable oxalate crystals within the marrow.

ddx.dx: Gaucher disease or other storage histiocytosis
ddx.vs: Storage disorders replace marrow with sheets of histiocytes with fibrillary ('crinkled paper') cytoplasm rather than extracellular refractile crystals with giant cells.

Immunoglobulin crystals are intracytoplasmic, eosinophilic and non-birefringent within histiocytes associated with a plasma cell or B-cell neoplasm, unlike the large extracellular birefringent oxalate rosettes.

captions: H&E, low-medium power: thickened trabeculae with fibrotic marrow containing rosettes of refractile crystals
H&E, high power: radiating colorless crystals surrounded by multinucleated foreign-body giant cells
Reticulin stain: markedly increased reticulin fibers around crystal-filled spaces
Polarized light: brightly birefringent radiating crystal aggregates (arrow)
